Lời mở đầu
DIGITAL ACCELERATION
          BREAKTHROUGH IN
THE RETAIL SECTOR
SAFETY - EFFICIENCY
2021 is a challenging year for the global economy in general and Vietnam’s 
economy in particular. The year 2021 marks the completion of MB’s development 
strategy for the period of 2017-2021 with the motto of “Digital acceleration, 
Breakthrough in the retail sector; Safety – Efficiency”. This is also a guideline to 
help MB overcome the pandemic impacts, proactively implement agile solutions 
around digital transformation, speeding up the journey to become the most 
convenient bank for all customers while ensuring safe and efficient growth.
DIGITAL ACCELERATION  
Striving to be the No. 1 Bank in Digital Banking in Vietnam, MB not only attracts talents in 
technology, but also invests heavily and applies the most advanced technologies, integrating 
multi- platforms in order to create the most updated and convenient digital experiences to both 
individual, corporate and institutional customers.
With a strong investment in technology and a customer-centric mindset, MB has been constantly 
innovating, providing the market with the best solutions for all financial and non-financial needs, 
creating a breakthrough in product development as well as business development scale, striving 
to be one of the Top 3 retail banks in Vietnam.
MB was one of the first banks to meet Basel II standards, applying many credit risk measurement 
models in professional activities, and effectively managing information technology risks and 
digital banking. In addition, MB always upholds compliance standards, respects the law, strictly 
abides by the provisions of the law and the State Bank, undeviatingly follows the required safety 
limits, ensures the sustainable and efficient development. In 2021, MB maintained the ranking of 
TOP 30 largest enterprises in Vietnam and was in the Top 20 enterprises with the best index of 
sustainable development in the market (VNSI - implemented by HSX in collaboration with PwC).
Despite of several challenges in 2021, with the efforts of the whole system and determination 
to implement the motto of “Digital acceleration, Breakthrough in the retail sector; Safety – 
Efficiency”, MB has achieved many great successes: Acquired 6.3 million new customers in 2021, 
equivalent to the accumulated number of customers MB has developed for 26 years since its 
establishment; successfully completed, outperformed most of the targets in terms of Scale, Profits, 
Customers, and Operational Efficiency. With the results achieved, MB continues to promote its 
strengths, flexibility and creativity to further improve service quality, increase experience and 
value for customers and shareholders; at the same time, affirms its leading position in the journey 
of transforming the Finance - Banking industry in Vietnam, creating a success momentum for the 
development strategy in the next periods.

INTRODUCTION

The world economic situation was heavily affected by 
the Covid- 19 pandemic and its new variants. The risks of 
inflation and political - economic tensions between world 
powers continued to increase. In particular, in the third 
quarter of 2021, Vietnam’s economy was seriously affected 
by the Delta variant, causing prolonged social distancing; 
and not until the fourth quarter of 2021 did it begin to 
recover thanks to effective vaccination and policies of the 
State and Government on safe adaptation to the pandemic. 
By the end of 2021, Vietnam’s GDP increased by 2.58% (the 
lowest increase in the last 10 years), however, Vietnam was 
among the top 20 economies in the world in terms of trade. 
The CPI was kept stable at ~ 1.84%, the lowest level since 
2016, the total investment of the entire society reached 
~ VND 2,892 million, 3.2% higher than in 2020. The State 
Bank of Vietnam continued operating a tight and flexible 
monetary policy in 2021: credit growth reached 13%, total 
customers’ accumulated interest exempted and reduced by 
credit institutions was ~ VND 34,9 trillion, exchange rates 
remained stable, non-performing loan (NPL) tended to 
increase but was under strict control.
In 2021, MB completed its development strategy 
for the period of 2017-2021 with the motto of 
“Digital acceleration, Breakthrough in the retail 
sector; Safety – Efficiency”, the vision of “The most 
convenient bank”, the effort to be “the No. 1 digital 
bank” and “the Top 3 retail banks in Vietnam”, 
which were set at the beginning of the year
The whole MB system, with a strong determination, 
successfully accomplished the strategic objectives and 
the tasks assigned by the General Shareholders Meeting, 
specifically:
•	 Total assets of the Group was VND 607,140 billion; Charter 
capital reached VND 37,783 billion, Profit before tax 
reached VND 16,527 billion (VND 14,398 billion from the 
Bank, VND 2,326 billion from the subsidiaries, accounting 
for 14% of the Group’s profit). (NPL ratio of the bank only 
was 0.68%, NPL coverage ratio was 349%), safe limits 
were in compliance with regulations of the State Bank; 
Performance indicators were reinforced: The Group’s ROE 
was 23.49% (the bank only accounted for 22.2%), CIR was 
33.06% (decreased 5% compared to 2020).
•	 In 2021, MB finished plan of 35% stock dividend, and 
continued to implement the plan to increase charter 
capital according, which was approved by the General 
Shareholders Meeting.
•	 MB’s digital transformation in 2021 marks many great 
successes, maintaining the leading position in the market: 
MB acquired 6.3 million new customers in 2021 (equivalent 
to the number of customers acquired in the last 26 years), 
more than 12.9 million customers in total. During the year, 
MB conducted ~390 million digital transactions (ranked 
first in Vietnam in December 2021); revenue from Digital 
Bank was ~ VND 3 trillion (2.5 times higher than in 2020). 
The bank has continuously improved and updated its 
digital capacity through ~260 new features on the App 
MBBank and the BIZ MBBank in 2021, applying state-of-
the-art technologies and solutions in the world to bring 
users the most fulfilling experience.
•	 In 2021, MB closed the Development Strategy for period of 
2017 - 2021 with excellent achievements in terms of Scale, 
Profit, Customers, and Operational Efficiency. Based on 
the great end results, consulting McKinsey on new global 
trends, MB has completed building and launching the MB 
Group Strategy for the 2022 - 2026 period.
•	 MB divisions have always conformed to and respected the 
law, actively participated in several gratitude programs, 
especially the social security activities, being recognized 
and trusted by the local people and authorities. In 
particular, in Q2 and Q3 of 2021, MB accompanied and 
supported the local government and military units in the 
prevention and control of the Covid-19 pandemic with a 
scale of nearly VND 400 billion and many other social 
security and gratitude programs.
In 2022, the world economy is forecast to grow at 
approximately 4% while Vietnam’s GDP and CPI at 6.5% 
and 3.5% - 3.8%, respectively, experiencing a strong 
recovery. Numerous sectors are expected to achieve better 
growth rate in 2022 including private property/FDI/customer 
consumption/retail/import - export/logistic. The State bank 
continues to operate a flexible monetary policy; credit is 
forecast to grow by ~ 13%; exchange rate is stabilized and 
NPL is strictly controlled.

In 2022, the State Bank’s capital adequacy ratio regulations 
are in effect, gearing towards Basel II standards.
2022 is the first year that the MB Group’s Strategy for period 
of 2022 - 2026 goes into effect with the motto of “Digital 
Acceleration - Customer Attraction - Group Synergy - 
Sustainable Reliability”, the vision of “To become a digital 
enterprise, a Leading Financial Group” and the goal of 
“Top 3 enterprises in terms of efficiency, striving to be the 
Top in Asia” by upholding the principle of “Respecting the 
law”; accordingly, MB will deploy new business models in 
Digital Banking as an important transformation of the 
new Strategy. Considering the challenging and regional-
level goals in the context of increasing competitiveness 
and potential difficulties after the Covid-19 pandemic, 
MB’s Board of Directors (BOD), Supervisory Board (SB), 
and Board of Management (BOM) are determined to 
make every effort to constantly grow, deploy flexible 
and innovative solutions to further improve MB’s service 
quality, increase experience, and attract customers to 
fulfill the strategic goal of the 2022 - 2026 period, adding 
more value to customers and shareholders, affirming MB’s 
pioneering and leading position in digital transformation 
of the Finance - Banking industry in Vietnam.
MB highly appreciates the existing and continuous 
direction and support of the Central Military Commission, 
the Ministry of National Defense, Ministries and agencies, 
and the support and cooperation from strategic partners 
and the trust of millions of customers, shareholders, and 
the dedicated efforts of 15,910 MB employees across 
the system. MB believes that, with your companionship 
and cooperation, MB will achieve the Bank’s goals and 
aspirations and will continue to bring more values to 
shareholders, the community and the society.

Message from
The Vice Chairman Cum
Chief Executive Officer
COVID- 19: A GOLDEN OPPORTUNITY FOR 
INNOVATION
In 2021, the Covid-19 pandemic continued to pose 
unprecedented challenges, seriously affecting the recovery 
of the global economy. Vietnam’s economy also experienced 
a turbulent year with the GDP growth rate of the whole year 
of only 2.58% (1) of the same period last year. However, this 
was still considered a positive result considering that in the 
third quarter of 2021, many key economic localities had 
to implement prolonged social distancing to prevent the 
pandemic.
Under these circumstances, MB actively developed scenarios 
and plans to deal with the pandemic, ensuring the health 
and mental well-being of 15,910 employees, maintaining an 
efficient, stable and smooth operation.
Turning the Covid-19 pandemic into an innovation “momentum”, 
MB focused on promoting digital transformation, identifying 
improvement of technology infrastructure capacity as a key 
factor. As a result, MB recorded impressive growth in 2021. 
Total profit before tax of the year reached VND 16,527 billion, 
increased 55% compared to 2020, completing 125% of the 
target approved by the 2021 General Shareholders Meeting.
NPL ratio maintained lower than the industry average. MB 
proactively booked provisions and maintained a high NPL 
coverage ratio of over 100%, ranking among the top banks 
in Vietnam, contributing more than VND 3 trillion to the State 
Budget. MB’s achievements accordingly became a highlight in 
the economy negatively affected by the Covid-19 pandemic.
MB maintained to be in the Top 30 largest enterprises in 
Vietnam (according to the VNR500 ranking), and won award 
of the Top 4 commercial banks in terms of scale and profit in 
Vietnam.
MB’s brand value increased to 113%, being one of the fastest 
growing global brand in 2022 (according to Brand Finance). 
This result reinforced MB’s reputation in the market despite 
the negative effects of the pandemic, and at the same time 
proved that MB’s move in the digital transformation strategy 
for period of 2017 - 2021 through several cooperation programs 
with leading technology companies such as Software AG in 
order to provide high- speed online services to customers was 
aggressive but steady.
“MB is determined to deliver on sustainable development goals”
SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT AT THE 
HEART
In 2021, MB firmly kept taking action toward the sustainable 
development goals, specifically in sustainable business, 
corporate governance, staff health and safety management, 
social responsibility, and protecting benefits of shareholders 
and investors.
MB has been standing side by side with businesses and 
communities in economic and life recovery in the complex 
context of the pandemic by providing a variety of appropriate 
financial and non-financial solutions. Particularly, MB was 
one of 16 joint stock commercial banks that agreed to 
reduce interest rates in accordance with Resolution 63/
NQ-CP of the Government and in the direction of the State 
Bank. As for the interest rate cuts for individuals, the bank 
also reduced the rate by 0.5-1.5 depending on the customer 
segment and the extent to which customers were affected 
by the pandemic.
Integrating social responsibility and social security in its 
business activities, in 2021, MB spent VND ~386 billion on 
community activities. The prevention measures of the Covid- 
19 pandemic only took VND 285 billion, and supported 38 
provinces and cities and 15 units nationwide.
With a practical approach, in 2021, MB was awarded one 
of the TOP 20 enterprises with the best sustainability 
index in the market (according to the evaluation of HSX 
in collaboration with PwC). This was MB’s statement on 
sustainable development goals in general, as well as the 
motto of “Digital acceleration, Breakthrough in the retail 
sector; Safety – Efficiency” for period of 2017-2021 in 
particular.
DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION JOURNEY 
SUCCESSFULLY NAVIGATED
MB made a strong mark on digital transformation in the 
past year, resulting in significant achievements: 258 new 
features were developed on the App MBBank, 391 million 
transactions were made on digital channels, 4.3 times 
higher than in 2020. MB’s fast inter-bank money transfer 
through the system of Vietnam National Finance Joint 
Stock Company ranked No. 1 in the market.
What made MB unique is its technological maturity 
and autonomy, along with a culture of experimenting, 
motivating employees to learn and be the best versions 
of themselves. This is an important factor that helps 
the bank go beyond the limitations of the traditional 
business model and create a unique value in the digital 
transformation race.
In 2021, MB gained strong group synergy. All of the 
subsidiaries grew in profits, contributing to the overall 
achievement of the whole group. Group revenue growth 
reached 35%. MIC ranked 1 level higher in market share, 
awarded the TOP 5 companies with the highest revenue. 
Mcredit also took a steady step up from TOP 4 to TOP 3 
in the market. In the past year, MB Ageas Life’s agencies 
scale rose 3 levels from TOP 12 to TOP 9.
BEGINNING A NEW STRATEGIC PERIOD
The year 2022 is forecasted to raise many unprecedented
risks and challenges. This is also the first year of the 
strategic period 2022-2026 where MB is striving for 
the goal of “Become a Digital Enterprise, a Leading 
Financial Group “ with the motto of “Digital Acceleration 
- Customer Attraction - Group Synergy - Sustainable 
Reliability” targeting “Top 3 efficient enterprises in the 
local market and Top enterprises in Asia”.
I believe that all the customers, shareholders, investors 
and staff will continue to accompany MB in 2022, the 
year of both opportunities and challenges.
Mr. Luu Trung Thai 
Vice Chairman of the BOD 
cum Chief Executive Officer

Development process
On 4 November 1994, Military Commercial Joint 
Stock Bank was established with the capital of 
nearly VND 20 billion, 25 employees and a single 
transaction office at 28A Dien Bien Phu Street, 
Hanoi.
The first ten years (1994-2004) was a necessary 
“exploration” period for MB to set the operating 
motto, build the business strategy and define 
the brand. Being determined with its long-term 
objectives and vision, MB confidently overcame 
the Asian financial crisis in 1997 and was the 
only bank that generated profit. In 2004, the 
year of its tenth anniversary of foundation, the 
total capital mobilization increased more than 
500 times compared to the initial amount; total 
assets reached more than VND 7 trillion; profits 
exceeded VND 500 billion; in the mean time, MB 
opened its new headquarters at No. 3 Lieu Giai 
Street, Ba Dinh District, Hanoi.
In 2010, MB started to develop the strategy for the 
new period 2011 – 2015, with an expectation to win 
the position in the top 3 joint stock commercial 
banks that are not predominantly owned by 
the State. On 1 November 2011, MB successfully 
listed MBB shares on the Ho Chi Minh City Stock 
Exchange.
This was also a very difficult period for the 
economy. The banking sector implemented a 
drastic restructuring process. In this context, 
MB remained steady in its sustainable and safe 
development strategy to win the leading position 
with respect to multiple financial indicators, and 
met its target of winning the position in the top 3 
list in 2013, two years ahead of schedule. In 2014, 
MB was honored to receive the First-Class Labour 
Medal for its achievements. Subsequently in 2015, 
MB was honored to be conferred the title “Hero of
Labor”.
During the period 2005-2009, MB adopted 
an array of comprehensive reform solutions: 
expanding the operation, developing network, 
investing 
in 
technology, 
strengthening 
its 
personnel, fousing on customers by differentiating 
the management function of the Head Office and 
the business function of branches, and dividing 
business units into private, SME, treasury and 
currency trading, etc.
This period was a solid foundation for MB to 
actively implement its strategic initiatives and 
become one of the Vietnamese leading financial 
institutions today. In 2009, MB celebrated its 
15th anniversary, awarded the Third-Class Labor 
Medal by the President of Vietnam.
During this time, MB has embraced the vision “To 
be the most convenient bank”. In particular, the 
goal of 2021 was to be one of the Top 5 Vietnamese 
banking systems in business efficiency, reliability, 
and digitalization.
In these years, despite many negative impacts 
of the Covid-19 pandemic, MB still experienced 
strong growth and breakthrough in business 
activities, successfully completing the tasks and 
targets. This period was highlighted by MB’s brand 
identity transformation into a more dynamic and 
youthful brand in 2019. MB was granted the Top 
2 most favorite brands; The brand value doubled, 
increased by 127 levels compared to 2020, making 
MB one of the Top 300 most valuable and 
powerful banking brands in the world (according 
to the Banking 500 2022 report of Brand Finance). 
MB was proud to maintain the TOP enterprises 
with a profit of over VND 10,000 billion and the 
TOP 5 banks by quality in Vietnam.
For 27 years of development, MB has affirmed its position 
as one of the leading banks in Vietnam, with the top 
effectiveness indicators in the market

- Governance (ESG) into 
the Company Policy
The Bank’s strategy was to maintain the traditional business model in parallel with 
integrating environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors into lending and 
investment activities. MB effectively allocated credit capital to serve the requirements 
of socio-economic development; promoted the development of “green credit”, “green 
bank” to transform the economy in green growth direction; increased the proportion 
of bank credit investment in renewable and clean energy.
MB has analyzed and completed the credit policy mechanism that is associated with 
environmental – social management, reviewed/updated the contents of the policy 
on environmental and social management in credit granting activities in line with 
MB’s operating model, built an annual credit granting orientation in which green 
credit growth is promoted as follows:
MB combined environmental and social risk management 
in the process of loan review and appraisal to control the 
funding for industries/fields with high environmental and 
social risks, and incorporated environmental risk assessment 
into credit risk assessment process. MB actively used the 
bank’s mobilized capital to grant credit to green sectors 
and at the same time seeked to applying for international 
green capital through financial institutions (such as World 
Bank, World Bank, Asian Development Bank (ADB), etc.) 
or through NGOs, or raised capital through green bonds 
for finance large-scale renewable energy projects and 
energy saving projects, etc. The bank also built a data 
system and an internal report system on the environmental 
compliance in accordance with the laws and orientations 
(i) Developed a set of Green Credit Statistical Indicators in 
accordance with the actual implementation situation and 
the reporting form according to Official Letter No. 9050/
NHNN-TD dated 3 November 2017;
(ii) Requested the set of criteria to be categorized by 
economic sectors, following Vietnam’s economic sector 
system regulated by the law, selecting green industries/
fields for credit granting
of the SBV, limiting loans approval for activities harmful 
to the environment. MB aimed for a data system on the 
envornmental compliance and violations of enterprises, 
creating a basis for credit institutions to appraise and grant 
credit, closely followed instructions of the SBV to promptly 
deploy and report in accordance with regulations.
Subsequently, MB is going to further review, improve and 
implement execution policies for the green credit goals, 
access to more loans support programs from international 
organizations and partners, contributing to greenhouse 
gas emissions reduction, thereby strongly promoting green 
growth and sustainable development.

The business projects such as Customer Insights, Smart Channels, Smart Marketing, 
Digital Lending, Customer Onboarding helped MB successfully attract more than 6

of customers acquired in the last 26 years from MB’s establishment), converting 
over 90% of total customer transactions into digital ones, making the proportion of 
income from digital channels to increase 2.2 times compared to 2020.

ADMINISTRATION
MB enhanced the quality of customer data and 
controlled the data by investing in modern Data 
management systems such as ODS, meta data and 
DWH optimization; completed policy frameworks 
for Data administration as well as data quality 
measurement tools. The bank also implemented 
Multi-Dimensional Profitability Analysis (MPA) 
project, helping analyze operational efficiency 
by business unit, customer, product, distribution 
channel, the basis for MB to effectively manage 
costs and optimize business operations.
FLEXIBLE IT INFRASTRUCTURE
Conducting digital transformation, MB has equipped itself with a modern and 
flexible information technology platform of 8 IT projects including Private Cloud, VDI, 
Consolidated Database, SDN, ITSM, DLP, Microservice and CRM Next Generation, 
ensuring system processing capacity, committing to a successful transaction rate of 
over 99%, meeting business requirements of over 20 million customers, reducing time 
to market, enhancing competencies for MB’s products and services.
SMART OPERATION
In 2021, by implementing Business Process Re-engineering 
(BPR) and Robotic Process Automation (RPA) projects, MB 
has significantly accelerated transaction processing speed 
for customers and internal processes, optimizing resources, 
and saving 70 FTEs.
SMART RISK MANAGEMENT
With PD project, MB completed building PD, LGD, and EAD 
models to meet Basel II and extensively applied the results 
into business activities, rasing the auto-approval rate for 
individual loans in 2021 to ~35%. MB also implemented 
ICAAP Project, helping the bank identify and manage 100% 
of the key risks on the software system, thereby optimizing 
capital allocation and risk-based pricing.

Overview of
the Corporate Governance
MB commits to practicing Corporate Governance (CG) in accordance with the applicable laws of 
Vietnam. In MB’s development strategy, MB refers to and manages to apply the best domestic and 
international practices in governance such as Vietnam’s Best Practices on Corporate Governance 
– VN CG Code and OECD Principles of CG, etc. MB always aims for efficiency, transparency, 
sustainable development and appropriateness in the development process. MB also refers to CG 
standards of the 2021 ASEAN CG Scorecard to self-assess and improve its corporate governance.
ASSESSMENT OF THE BOD ON MB’S PERFORMANCE
According to a report from the General Statistics Office, Vietnam’s GDP in 2021 grew by 
2.58% (lower than GDP growth in 2020 and the target level of 6.5% set by the Government 
at the beginning of the year) because the Covid-19 epidemic has seriously affected all 
areas of the economy - many key localities had to implement prolonged social distancing 
to prevent the disease. The negative growth of some service industries which accounted for 
a large proportion of the total sector reduced the overall growth rate of the service sector 
and the entire economy. The banking industry has faced many challenges: On one hand 
it has had to actively maintain its financial capacity, has significantly reduced operating 
costs to support businesses and individuals through interest rates reduction as directed by 
the State Bank (banks had already waived, reduced, and lowered interest rates for over 
1.96 million customers affected by the pandemic with outstanding loans of more than 
VND 3,870 trillion; total accumulated interest waived, reduced or lowered for customers 
was about VND 34,900 billion; from 23 January 2020 to the end of 2021, the accumulated 
revenue difference of new loans and those before the pandemic reached over VND 
7,400 trillion for about over 1.3 million customers); On the other hand, the industry has 
faced potential NPLs when clients’ businesses slowed down. The State Bank continued to 
implement solutions to control credit limit, and at the same time improved credit quality; 
as a result, the operation of the banking system in general achieved positive results: the 
deposit with credit institutions increased by 8.44%, credit growth of the economy reached 
12.97%.
2021 was the last year of implementing the 2017-2021 Development Strategy. After more 
than 2 years of efforts and determination, with proactive and flexible solutions to overcome 
the effects of the Covid-19 pandemic, focus on Digital Transformation and cost savings, 
MB made a substantial transformation on the market while sticking to its direction of 
“To become the most convenient bank,” and completed the strategic goal of being 
“TOP 5 in terms of business efficiency and safety” with solid growth of several business 
indicators. In particular, after 5 years, the number of customers increased by more than 4 
times, outstanding loans increased by 2.4 times, deposits increased 2 times, profit before 
tax increased ~ 4 times, the average annual NPL ratio was strictly controlled at ~ 1.1%. 
The synchronous and drastic implementation of 4 key transformations (Digital banking, 
Improvement of customers’ relationships, Outstanding risk management, Enhancement 
of operational efficiency of subsidiaries) helped MB create significant imprints. The App 
MBBank and the BIZ MBBank platforms attracted an extraordinary number of customers 
on the market (the number of customers converted to MB’s digital channels reached over 6 
million people, exceeding the strategic target with the number of transactions conducted 
on digital channels equivalent to that of top banks in Asia). The quality of customer 
relationship has been improved as demonstrated by the increased productivity of RMs in 
all three segments of Retail, SME and CIB with the customer satisfaction rate of over 80%. 
MB was one of the first banks to meet Basel II standards and effectively apply various 
credit risk assessment models in credit activities, information risks management and 
digital banking. As the parent company, MB has strengthened the corporate governance 
model of the group. Accordingly, profits of subsidiaries grew strongly compared to 2016 
and contributed significantly to the group’s profit.

Internal Audit Department is a division-level department, organized at the Head 
Office, directly under the SB’s control and under the direct direction of the SB. The 
Internal Audit Department is the third line of defense in the 3-line defense model, 
conducting an independent review of the performance of the first and second lines 
of defense; performing audits on the supervision of senior management over the 
BOD, the CEO; reporting directly to the BOD, the SB in accordance with the laws 
and internal regulations of MB; reporting indirectly to the BOM and related parties. 
The Internal Audit Department is also a unit with the function of group management, 
leading, orienting, providing training and supporting to advance the internal audit 
capacity in the whole group.
Auditing activities are planned annually on the principle of risk orientation, whereby 
high-risk activities will be receiving more resources and higher prioritization of audit 
activities as compared to lower risk activities.
Internal audit process:
In 2021, the Internal Audit Department proactively implemented and completed audit 
programs as planned.
The audit results promptly pointed out the key shortcomings that needed improvement, 
which were recognized and highly appreciated by the BOD and departments; all 
the recommendations/advices were promptly executed by the departments, thereby 
contributing to the improvement and enhancement of MB’s operational quality.
In 2022, the Internal Audit Department will carry out activities in the direction of 
transforming internal audit capacity in association with MB’s strategic orientation for 
the period ]2022-2026: “Become a Digital Enterprise, a Leading Financial Group”. The 
Internal Audit Department developed audit capacity and added advisory value to 
the group’s operations while ensured compliance with laws and internal regulations.
In addition to the periodical audit programs as regulated, the audit plan for 2022 
continues to focus on high-risk activities/departments at Headquarters, Branches 
and Subsidiaries.
The Internal Audit Department performs independent and objective review and 
assessment of the internal control system; independent assessment of the adequacy 
and compliance with established regulations, internal policies, procedures, and 
processes; making recommendations to improve the efficiency of systems, processes 
and regulations, contributing to assurance of MB’s safe, effective and lawful operation.
The Internal Audit Department operates on the principles of independence, objectivity, 
and professionalism.
Internal auditors do not concurrently undertake the tasks and responsibilities of 
individuals and departments that are subject to the Internal Audit Department; 
are not subject to any interference while performing the reporting and evaluation 
duties. The audit notes in the Internal Audit reports are carefully analyzed and based 
on collected data and information. Internal auditors ensure honesty when making 
reports and evaluations during the internal audit process. Internal auditors have the 
necessary knowledge, qualifications and skills as required by regulations, and at the 
same time ensure compliance with the law in performing assigned tasks.

effort of MB to bring value to shareholders by ensuring a regular annual dividend 
payment, even in the difficult business situation as impacted by the Covid-19 
epidemic in 2021.

Smart, outstanding risk management has always been a key foundation in MB’s 
strategic stages. This is also an important transformation in the group of 4 strategic 
transformations of MB in the period 2017-2021. MB has completed all 3 pillars of Basel 
II early, in compliance with Circular 41 and Circular 13 of the State Bank of Vietnam, 
with independent assessment by Ernst & Young. MB focuses on building a scientific 
Internal Control system, intelligent risk management associated with “models, tools, 
data” which enables rapid growth and risk control.
The process of implementing the risk management platform is implemented by 
MB consistently and thoroughly. MB proactively researches, applies and refines risk 
management platform. Basel II helped MB achieve its goals of credit growth of over 
20% in recent years, ensuring safety targets as of 31 December 2021, NPL ratio was 
<1% (at 0.68% for single and 0.90% for consolidated balance sheet), NPL coverage 
ratio was 349%, capital adequacy ratio was 11.28% (compared to the minimum 
requirement of 8%).
The role of high-level supervision and the 3 lines of defense model as required 
in Circular 13 of the State Bank and the Basel Committee’s practices, has been 
comprehensively and effectively applied by MB in management activities and internal 
control of the bank. MB standardizes the responsibilities of the BOD and the CEO for 
internal control activities, risk management, assessment of capital adequacy, and 
internal audit activities, ensuring the independent role, an individual/unit does not 
simultaneously participate in the “executive” and the “administrative” function.
MB organizes the entire management system through the application of the 3 lines 
of defense model to ensure a clear separation of functions and tasks of the units, 
increases the Bank’s sense of responsibility in identifying, assessing, monitoring, and 
controlling risks. In particular, processes which have potential conflict of interest 
(sales, appraisal, approval and operation) are performed by independent units, 
ensuring objectivity and transparency. At the same time, in order to well control risks 
and limit errors caused by errors/intentional violations, MB has applied advanced 
technology systems, centralized at Head Office the following functions: appraisal, 
approval, operation; accounting – finance, human resources, information technology. 
Accordingly, MB’s branches and business units are freed up for business development, 
but still ensure that risks are well controlled when the business scale and transaction 
volume/number of customers widens.

At MB, risk management always means robust application

banking, retail transformation).
MB has established 42 risk models for all customer 
segments (Including Credit rating scorecard models 
(A-score, B-score, Rating); PD (Probability of default); LGD 
(Loss Given Default) and EAD (Exposure At Default)). These 
models having passed stringent tests and hence are highly 
reliable, assist optimization and automation of the entire 
process of credit granting.	
•	 The results of the A Score, B Score using scorecard model 
are applied to the process of credit selection, appraisal, 
approval, and standardization of forms for segments, 
especially individual customers, and small SMEs.
•	 The results of the PD, LGD, and LGD models are applied 
to calculate the estimated loss, measure specifically the 
benefits from each customer, and balance it with the 
estimated risks of the customer.
•	 Early Warning Signal model allows to identify customers 
showing signs of financial deterioration impacting timely 
repayment ability, and hence appropriate solutions to 
assist customers to recover and/or collect debt could be 
made.

customer contact, appraisal, approval, loan monitoring 
and debt collection. At the same time, it connects to

RISK MANAGEMENT
Environmental and social risks are managed according to MB’s General Risk 
Management Framework, similar to other types of risks, mentioned in the Risk 
Management section in page 124.
According to the direction of the Government and the SBV, MB has analyzed and 
completed the credit policy mechanism associated with environmental – social 
management, reviewed/updated the contents of the policy on environmental and 
social management in credit granting activities in line with MB’s operating model, 
built an annual credit granting orientation in which green credit growth is promoted 
as follows:
•	 Developed a set of Green Credit Statistical Indicators in accordance with the actual 
implementation situation and the reporting form according to Official Letter No. 
9050/NHNN-TD dated 03 November 2017;
•	 Requested the set of criteria to be categorized by economic sectors, following 
Vietnam’s economic sector system regulated by the law, selecting green industries/
fields for credit granting.
MB combines environmental and social risk management in the process of loan 
review and appraisal to control and limit the funding for industries/fields with high 
environmental and social risks. The Bank aims for improving investment portfolio, 
granting credit through a more advanced and upgraded environmental and social 
risk management system which can assess project’s impact on environment - 
society, and assessing environmental and social security risks of the project before 
granting credit.
The credit granting process always considers the combination of the appraisal of 
projects and loan plans, environmental protection and authorities’ certification for 
compliance with the regulations on technology standards in order to limit/control 
projects that are likely to have a great impact on the environment - society.
In the coming time, MB will continue to build and appoint a specialized department 
within the Risk Management Division to deploy green credit banking activities, 
manage and assess environmental and social risks in accordance with the direction 
of the Government and the State Bank.

Military Commercial Joint Stock Bank (“the Bank”) is a joint stock commercial bank 
incorporated and registered in the Socialist Republic of Vietnam.
The Bank was established under Operating Licence No. 100/NH-GP granted by the 
Governor of the State Bank of Vietnam (“the SBV”) dated 17 October 2018, replacing 
Operating License No. 0054/NH-GP dated 14 September 1994. The operating 
duration under the licence is 99 years from the date of 14 September 1994. The 
Bank is operating under Business Registration No. 0100283873 granted by the 
Hanoi Department of Planning and Investment on 30 September 1994 and the 49th 
amended Business Registration on 25 August 2021. 
The current principal activities of the Bank are to perform banking services including 
mobilizing and receiving short, medium and long-term deposits from organizations 
and individuals; making short, medium and long-term loans to organizations and 
individuals based on the nature and capability of the Bank’s capital; conducting 
foreign exchange transactions, international trade finance services, discounting of 
commercial papers, bonds and other valuable papers; providing settlement services 
and other banking services as approved by the SBV.

(31 December 2020: VND27,987,569 million).

2.1. FISCAL YEAR
MB’s fiscal year starts on 1 January and ends on 31 December.
2.2. ACCOUNTING CURRENCY
The currency used in the preparation of financial statements of MB is Vietnam Dong (“VND”). 
For the purpose of preparing the consolidated financial statements as at 31 December 2021, all 
amounts are rounded to the nearest million and presented in VND million. The presentation makes 
no impact on readers’ view of the consolidated financial position, consolidated income statement 
and consolidated cash flows of MB.
3.1. STATEMENT OF COMPLIANCE 
Management of MB confirms that the accompanying consolidated financial statements have 
been prepared in accordance with Vietnamese Accounting Standards, Vietnamese Accounting 
System for Credit Institutions and statutory requirements relevant to preparation and presentation 
of consolidated financial statements.
3.2. ACCOUNTING STANDARDS AND SYSTEM 
The consolidated financial statements of MB are prepared in accordance with the accounting 
system applicable to credit institutions under Decision No. 479/2004/QD-NHNN dated 29 
April 2004 on promulgating the chart of credit institutions and amending and supplementing 
regulations of Decision No. 479/2004/QD-NHNN; Decision No. 16/2007/QD-NHNN dated 18 April 
2007 on the issuance of the financial reporting mechanism for credit institutions and amending 
and supplementing regulations of Decision No. 16/2007/QD-NHNN and Vietnamese Accounting 
Standards issued by the Ministry of Finance as per:

Four Vietnamese Accounting Standards (Series No.1);
•	 Decision No. 165/2002/QD-BTC dated 31 December 2002 on the Issuance and Promulgation of 
Six Vietnamese Accounting Standards (Series No.2);
•	 Decision No. 234/2003/QD-BTC dated 30 December 2003 on the Issuance and Promulgation of 
Six Vietnamese Accounting Standards (Series No.3); 
•	 Decision No. 12/2005/QD-BTC dated 15 February 2005 on the Issuance and Promulgation of Six 
Vietnamese Accounting Standards (Series No. 4); and
•	 Decision No. 100/2005/QD-BTC dated 28 December 2005 on the Issuance and Promulgation of 
Four Vietnamese Accounting Standards (Series No.5).
 
Accordingly, the accompanying consolidated financial statements and their utilization are not 
designed for those who are not informed about Vietnam’s accounting principles, procedures and 
practices and furthermore are not intended to present the consolidated financial position and results 
of consolidated operations and consolidated cash flows in accordance with accounting principles 
and practices generally accepted in countries other than Vietnam.
Items or balances required by Decision No. 16/2007/QD-NHNN and amending, supplementing 
regulations issued by the SBV regarding the financial statements reporting mechanism for credit 
institutions that are not shown in these consolidated financial statements indicate nil balance.
3.3. ASSUMPTIONS AND USES OF ESTIMATES
The preparation of the consolidated financial statements requires Management to make estimates 
and assumptions that affect the reported amount of assets and liabilities and disclosure of 
contingent liabilities. These estimates and assumptions also affect the income, expenses and 
the resultant provisions. Such estimates are necessarily based on assumptions involving varying 
degrees of subjectivity and uncertainty and actual results may differ, resulting in future changes 
in such provision.
3.4. BASIS OF CONSOLIDATION
	
The consolidated financial statements comprise the financial statements of the Bank and its 
subsidiaries for the year ended 31 December 2021.
Subsidiaries are fully consolidated from the acquisition date, on which the Bank obtains control 
and continue to be consolidated until the Bank terminates the control.
The financial statements of the Bank and its subsidiaries are prepared for the same reporting 
period, using consistent accounting policies.
All intra-company balances, income and expenses and unrealized gains or losses resulting from 
intra-company transactions are eliminated in full.
Non-controlling interest represents the portion of net results of operations and net assets not 
owned, either directly or indirectly through the subsidiaries, by MB and are presented separately 
in the consolidated income statement and within equity in the consolidated balance sheet, 
separately from the Bank’s equity and liabilities.

Cash and cash equivalents comprise cash, current accounts at the State Banks, Government bills

Placements with and loans to other credit institutions are presented at the principal amounts

4.4. LOANS TO CUSTOMERS 
Loans to customers are presented at the principal amounts outstanding at the reporting date. 
Provision for credit losses of loans to customers is accounted and presented in a separate line in 
the consolidated balance sheet.
Short-term loans have maturity of less than one year from disbursement date. Medium-term loans 
have maturity from one to five years from disbursement date. Long-term loans have maturity of 
more than five years from disbursement date.
Loan classification and provision for credit losses are made according to Circular 11/2021 as 
presented in Note 4.5.

4.6. DEBT TRADING
Debt trading activities of the Bank are recorded in accordance with Circular 09/2015/TT-NHNN 
(“Circular 09/2015”) of SBV regulating debt trading by credit institutions, foreign bank branches.
•	 Book value of a purchased and sold debt includes the book value of debt principal and interest 
and other debt-related financial obligations (if any) by the time of debt purchase and sale for 
the debt accounted on the balance sheet or off the balance sheet; or the book value being 
monitored at the time of being removed off the balance sheet or at the time of debt purchase 
and sale for the debt being removed off the balance sheet;
•	 Debt purchase and sale price means a sum of money to be paid by a debt purchaser to a debt 
seller under a debt purchase and sale contract.
Debt purchase
For the purchased debts, the Bank classifies the paid amount into a group with risk level not 
lower than previous debt group that was classified before the purchase. Debt classification and 
provision for debt purchases are made similar to loans to other customers according to Circular 
11/2021.
•	 The price of debt purchase under the contract is accounted on the balance sheet;
•	 The value of principal and interest of purchased debt is monitored off the balance sheet;
•	 If the interest of the debt including the interest before the purchase is collected, the Bank will 
allocate the interest on the following principle: (i) write down the value of debt purchase by 
pre-purchase interest; (ii) recognize as interest income of the period after the Bank purchases 
the debt.
Debt sale
Revenue and expense from selling debts are recorded in accordance with Circular 09/2015, where 
the difference between the debt purchase, sale price and debt seller’s book value is handled as 
follows:
•	 For the debts being recorded on the balance sheet:
‐‐ If the debt sale price is higher than the book value of the debt, the difference shall be 
accounted as income of the Bank during the period.
‐‐ If the debt sale price is lower than the value of the debt, the difference shall be offset with the 
compensation paid by an individual or an organization (in case such individual or organization 
is identified to have caused the damage and must pay compensation under regulations), the 
insurance sum paid by the insurer or the risk provision already set aside from expenses; the 
deficit shall be accounted as a business cost of the Bank.
For the debt accounted off the balance sheet or debt left off the balance sheet, the debt sale 
proceeds shall be accounted as other income of the Bank.
4.7. SECURITIES HELD FOR TRADING
Securities held for trading include debt securities, equity securities and other securities acquired 
and held for the purpose of trading. Securities held for trading are initially recognized at cost.
Listed debt securities held for trading are recognized at cost less provision for diminution in value 
of securities, which is based on the yield quoted on the Hanoi Stock Exchange at the balance 
sheet date. 
Provision for credit losses of corporate bonds, which are not listed on the stock market or not 
registered on the unlisted public company market, is made in accordance with Circular 11/2021 as 
described in Note 4.5.
Equity securities are recognized at cost. Periodically, provision for impairment of securities held for 
trading is recorded when their book values are higher than their market values. In case the market 
values of the securities cannot be determined, no provision is made. Provision for impairment is 
recognized in the interim consolidated income statement as “Net gain from securities held for 
trading”.
Gains or losses from sales of securities held for trading are recognized in the interim consolidated 
income statement. Securities held for trading are derecognized when the rights to receive cash 
flows from these securities are terminated or MB transfers substantially all the risks and rewards 
of ownership of these securities.

4.8. INVESTMENT SECURITIES
 
4.8.1. Available-for-sale investment securities
Available-for-sale investment securities include debt and equity securities that are acquired by 
MB for the investment and available-for-sale purposes, not regularly traded but can be sold when 
there is a benefit. 
Available-for-sale equity securities are securities listed on securities markets. They are initially 
recognized at cost at the purchase date and continuously presented at cost in subsequent periods.
Available-for-sale debt securities are recognized at par value at the transaction date. Accrued 
interest (for debt securities with interest payment in arrears) and deferred interest (for debt 
securities with interest payment in advance) is recognized in a separate account. Discount/
premium, which is the difference between the cost and the amount being the par value plus 
(+) accrued interest (if any) or minus (-) deferred interest (if any) is also recognized in a separate 
account. 
In subsequent periods, these securities are continuously recorded at par value, and the discount/
premium (if any) is amortized to the consolidated income statement on a straight-line basis over 
the remaining term of securities. The interest received in arrears is recorded as follows: Cumulative 
interest incurred before the purchase date is recorded as a decrease in the accrued interest; 
cumulative interest incurred after the purchase date is recognized as income based on the 
accumulated method. The interest received in advance is amortized into interest income on a 
straight-line basis over the term of investment securities.
Available-for-sale securities are subject to impairment review on a periodical basis.
	
	
Provision for diminution in value of securities is made when the carrying value is higher than the 
market value. Provision is recognized in the “Net gain/(loss) from investment securities and long-term 
investments” of the consolidated income statement.
Provision for credit losses of corporate bonds which are not listed on the stock market or not 
registered on the unlisted public companies market is made in accordance with Circular 11/2021 
as described in Note 4.5.
4.8.2. Held-to-maturity investment securities
Held-to-maturity securities are debt securities purchased by MB for the investment purpose of 
earning interest and MB has the capability and intention to hold these investments until maturity. 
Held-to-maturity securities have determined value and maturity dates. In case the securities are 
sold before the maturity date, the remaining portfolio of these securities will be reclassified to 
securities held-for-trading or available-for-sale securities.
Held-to-maturity securities are recorded and measured identically to debt available-for-sale 
securities and presented at Note 4.8.1.
 
4.9. OTHER LONG-TERM INVESTMENTS
Other long-term investments are investments in other entities in which MB holds less than or 
equal 11% of voting rights and securities of these entities are not listed on the stock market. These 
investments are initially recorded at cost at the transaction date.
Provision for diminution in the value of investment is made when there is substantial evidence 
indicating a decline in the value of these investments at the balance sheet date.
The provision is reversed if the recoverable amount of the investments increases after making 
provision, to the extent that the carrying value of these investments does not exceed the carrying 
value of the investments assuming that no allowance has been recorded.
 
Increase or decrease in provision for long-term investments is recognized in “Net gain/ (loss) from 
investment securities and long-term investments” on the consolidated income statement.
4.10. FIXED ASSETS
	
	
Fixed assets are stated at cost less accumulated depreciation or amortization. 
The cost of a fixed asset comprises its purchase price plus any directly attributable costs of 
bringing the asset to working condition for its intended use. 
Cost related to additions, improvements and renewals are capitalized while expenditures for 
maintenance and repairs are charged to the consolidated income statement.
When assets are sold or liquidated, their cost and accumulated depreciation/amortisation are 
deducted from the consolidated balance sheet and any gains or losses resulting from their 
disposal (being the difference between net proceeds from the sale of assets and the remaining 
value of assets) are recorded to the consolidated income statement.

4.12. INVESTMENT PROPERTIES
4.12.1. Investment rental properties 
Investment properties held for rental are stated as cost less accumulated depreciation. The 
initial cost of investment rental property includes the purchase price, cost of land use rights, and 
directly attributable costs of bringing the asset to the condition necessary for the asset to function 
properly. Expenses incurred after the rental investment property have been put into operation, 
such as repairs and maintenance, are recognized in the consolidated statement of income in 
the period in which they are incurred. In cases where it can be clearly demonstrated that these 
expenses increase the expected future economic benefits from the investment property in excess 
of its initialy assessed standard performance, these costs are capitalized as an increase in cost of 
investment rental property.
Depreciation is calculated using the straight-line method over the estimated useful lives of the 
investment properties. The estimated useful life of land use rights and assets on land is 39 years 
and assets attached to land is 20 years.
4.12.2. Investment properties held for capital appreciation
Investment properties held for capital appreciation are stated at cost less any devaluation in 
market prices. The carrying amount of an investment property held for capital appreciation 
is reduced when there is evidence that its market price fell below its carrying amount and the 
loss can be measured reliably. Any reduction in value of investment properties held for capital 
appreciation is charged to the consolidated income statement.  
4.13. RECEIVABLES
	
4.13.1. Receivables classified as credit risk-bearing assets 
	
Receivables classified as credit risk-bearing assets are recognized at cost and classified and 
provided for allowance by MB in accordance with Article 10 of Circular 11/2021 and presented in 
Note 4.5.
4.13.2. Other receivables
	
Receivables other than credit risk-bearing assets of MB are initially recorded at cost and always 
carried at cost subsequently.

4.14. PREPAID EXPENSES AND DEFERRED EXPENSES
Prepaid expenses are reported as short-term or long-term ones on the consolidated balance 
sheet and amortized over the period for which the amount is paid or the period in which economic 
benefit is generated in relation to these expenses.
4.15. BUSINESS COMBINATIONS AND GOODWILL
Business combinations are accounted for using the acquisition method. The cost of a business 
combination is measured as the fair value of assets given, equity instruments issued and liabilities 
incurred or assumed at the date of business combination plus any costs directly attributable to 
the business combination. Identifiable assets and liabilities and contingent liabilities assumed in 
a business combination of the acquiree are measured initially at fair value at the date of business 
combination. 
Goodwill acquired in a business combination is initially recognized at cost being the excess of the 
cost of the business combination over the acquirer’s interest in the net fair value of the acquiree’s 
identifiable assets, liabilities and contingent liabilities. If the cost of a business combination is 
less than the fair value of the net assets of the subsidiary acquired, the difference is recognized 
directly to the consolidated income statement. After initial recognition, goodwill is measured at 
cost less any accumulated amortization. Goodwill is amortized in ten (10) years on a straight-line 
basis.
4.16. RE-PURCHASE AND REVERSE RE-PURCHASE CONTRACTS
Securities sold under agreements to repurchase at a specific date in the future (repos) are still 
recognized in the consolidated financial statements. The corresponding cash received from these 
agreements is recognized in the consolidated balance sheet as a borrowing and the difference 
between the sale price and repurchase price is amortized in the consolidated income statement 
over the term of the agreement using the straight-line method based on the interest rate stipulated 
in the contract.
	
Conversely, securities purchased under agreements to resell at a specific date in the future are not 
recognized in the consolidated financial statements. The corresponding cash paid under these 
agreements is recognized as a loan in the consolidated balance sheet and the difference between 
the purchase price and resale price is amortized in the consolidated income statement over the 
term of the agreement using the straight-line method based on the interest rate stipulated in the 
contract.

he determination of whether an arrangement is, or contains a lease is based on the substance of

Rentals under operating leases are charged to the consolidated income statement on a straight-line

Assets subject to operating leases are included as MB’s fixed assets in the consolidated balance

4.19. DEPOSITS FROM OTHER CREDIT INSTITUTIONS AND CUSTOMERS, OTHER BORROWED 
AND ENTRUSTED FUNDS AND VALUABLE PAPERS ISSUED
Deposits from other credit institutions, customer deposits, other borrowed and entrusted funds 
and valuable papers issued are disclosed at the principal amounts outstanding at the end of 
the financial year. Valuable papers issued are initially recognized at cost at face value deducting

According to accounting system of MB, all transactions are recorded in original currencies. 
Monetary assets and liabilities denominated in foreign currencies are translated into VND using

arising in foreign currencies during the period are converted into VND at rates ruling at the 
transaction dates. Foreign exchange differences arising from the translation of monetary assets 
and liabilities are recognized in the consolidated income statement.

Payables and accruals are recognized for amounts to be paid in the future for goods and services 
received, whether or not billed to MB.

Covered call warrants are secured securities issued by MB Securities Joint Stock Company, a

(ii) Mathematical reserve
Mathematical reserve is the difference between the present value of total insurance payables 
in the future and the present value of the net insurance premiums with Zillmer adjustment for 
insurance premiums receivables in the future. Mathematical reserve is calculated for insurance 
policies that have valid period of more than one (1) year with specific actuarial formulae and 
factors for each type of products as registered and approved by the Ministry of Finance. The 
maximum valuation interest rate is linked to the average interest rate of government bonds as per 
formula specified in the Circular 01/2019/TT-BTC.
(iii) Claims reserve
Claims reserve includes reserve for claims outstanding at the end of the period but not yet resolved 
and for claims incurred but not reported.
•	 Outstanding claim reserve is established based on the estimated claim payments for each claim 
for which the insurer is liable, which is either notified to the insurer or requested for payment 
but is still unresolved at the end of the fiscal year after deducting the amount recoverable from 
reinsurers; and
•	 Reserve for incurred but not reported claims for which the insurer is liable (IBNR) is established 
according to regulations in Circular 50.
	
Gross and assumed reinsurance claim reserve is presented as liabilities; claim reserve of ceded 
reinsurance is presented in “Other commitments“.
(iv) Catastrophe reserve
Catastrophe reserve is made annually until it reaches 100% of the retained premiums of the 
accounting period and based on the rate of retained premiums according to Circular 50. 
On 28 December 2005, the Ministry of Finance issued Decision No. 100/2005/QD-BTC governing 
the publication of four new accounting standards, including Vietnamese Accounting Standard 
(“VAS”) 19 – Insurance Contract. Accordingly, from January 2006, the provision of catastrophe 
reserve is no longer required since it represents “possible claims under contracts that do not exist 
at the reporting date”. However, since the Ministry of Finance has not issued detailed guidance 
for the implementation of VAS 19 and according to Decree No. 73/2016/ND-CP issued by the 
Government of Vietnam dated 1 July 2016 on details of the implementation of the Law on Insurance 
Business and amendments to certain articles of the Law on Insurance Business (“Decree 73”), MB 
continues to make catastrophe reserve on the consolidated financial statements for the fiscal 
year ended 31 December 2021.
(v) Equalization reserve 
The reserve is set aside one percent (1%) of its profit before tax annually for reserve until this 
reserve reaches five percent (5%) collected premiums in the fiscal year of MB Ageas Life Insurance 
Company Limited.

4.25. RECOGNITION OF INCOME AND EXPENSES
Income and expenses from banking operation
Interest income and expenses are recognized in the consolidated income statement on an accrual 
basis. The recognition of accrued interest income of a loan in the consolidated income statement 
is suspended for loans classified in groups 2 to 5 in compliance with Circular 11/2021 and loans 
restructured according to Circular 01. Suspended interest income is reversed and monitored off-
balance sheet and recognized in the consolidated income statement upon actual receipt.
Fees and commissions are recognized when the services are performed.
For other income, when the result of the contract is definitely determined, income is recognized 
based on the stage of completion of work or service. If the result of the contract is not determined, 
income is only recognized to the extent of recoverable amount of expenses incurred.
According to Circular No. 16/2018/TT-BTC dated 7 February 2018 by the Ministry of Finance 
guiding some articles on financial regime for credit institution, foreign bank branch, receivables 
from uncollectible accrued income at the due date are recorded as reduction in revenue if the 
income has been accrued in the same accounting period or recorded as expense if the income 
has been accrued in different accounting periods and monitored off-balance sheet. Upon actual 
receipt of these receivables, MB would recognize to “Other income” on the consolidated income 
statement.
Income from securities trading business
Income from securities trading is determined by the difference between the selling price and the 
weighted average cost of the securities.
Cash dividends are recognized in the consolidated statement of income when the right to receive 
cash dividends of MB is established. Dividends received in the form of common shares, bonus 
shares and stock options for current shareholders, shares distributed from undistributed profits 
are not recognized as an income of MB but only update the number of stock.
Income from insurance business
Gross written premiums are recognized in accordance with Circular 50/2017/TT-BTC.
Income from real estate business
	
Income is recognized to the extent that it is probable that the economic benefits will flow to MB. 
Income is measured at the fair value of the consideration received or receivable, excluding trade 
discount, rebate and sales returned. 
Income is recognised when MB has passed significant risks and rewards associated with the 
apartments to the buyers and income can be reliably measured.
Claim expenses for insurance activities
Claim expenses of gross premium is recognized on the basis of incurrence when insurance 
companies accept claims.
Claim expenses for reinsurance premiums assumed is recognized upon incurrence in accordance 
with the statement of the reinsurer which was sent to the insurance companies and accepted by 
these companies.
Claim receivables for reinsurance premiums ceded are recognized upon actual incurrence in 
accordance with the receivable amount corresponding to claim expense recognized during the 
period and the rate of reinsurance ceded.
Other expenses for insurance activities are recognized when incurred.
Commission expenses for insurance business
Commission is calculated at certain percentage of direct premiums for specific line of insurance as 
stipulated in Circular 50. Commission expenses are allocated and recognized in the consolidated 
income statement for direct premiums earned during the period. The commission which is not 
allocated would be recognized as prepaid expense and being allocated in the subsequent periods.
Loan origination costs from loan to customers in the finance company
Loan origination costs including commissions to agencies, third parties, and sale personnel 
are amortized into the consolidated income statement using the straight-line method over the 
average duration of the loan product types ranging from 9 - 29 months.
4.26. CORPORATE INCOME TAXES
Current income tax
Current income tax assets and liabilities for the current and prior periods are measured at the 
amount expected to be recovered from (or paid to) the taxation authorities - using the tax rates 
and tax laws applied and enacted at the consolidated balance sheet date. 
Current income tax is charged or credited to the consolidated income statement except when it 
relates to items recognized directly to equity, in this case the current income tax is also recognized 
in equity.
Current income tax assets and liabilities are offset when there is a legally enforceable right for MB 
to offset current tax assets against current tax liabilities and when MB intends to settle its current 
tax assets and liabilities on a net basis.

4.26. CORPORATE INCOME TAXES (continued)
Deferred tax
Deferred tax is provided on temporary differences at the consolidated balance sheet date 
between the tax base of assets and liabilities and their carrying amount for the financial reporting 
purposes. 
Deferred tax payables are recognized for temporary taxable differences.
Deferred tax assets are recognized for all deductible temporary differences, deductible amounts 
carried over subsequent periods of taxable losses and unused tax credits when it is probable that 
there will be sufficient taxable profit to use deductible temporary differences, taxable losses and 
tax credits. The carrying amount of deferred tax assets must be reviewed at the balance sheet 
date and the carrying amount of the deferred tax asset is reduced to the extent that it is probable 
that sufficient profit will be available to allow for the benefit of all or part of a deferred tax asset 
to be used. Previously unrecognized deferred tax assets are reviewed at the balance sheet date 
and recognized to the extent that it is probable that future taxable profit will be available against 
which to use the assets.
Deferred tax assets and deferred tax liabilities are determined on the basic of expected tax rate 
applied when assets are recovered or liabilities are settled and on the basis of tax rate and tax 
laws which effective at the end of the period.
4.27. CLASSIFICATION FOR OFF-BALANCE-SHEET COMMITMENTS
According to Circular 11/2021, credit institutions should classify guarantees, payment acceptances 
and irrevocable loan commitments with specific effective date (generally called “off-balance sheet 
commitments”) in compliance with Article 10, Circular 11/2021 for management and monitoring of 
credit quality. Accordingly, off-balance sheet commitments are classified into groups which are 
Current, Special Mention, Substandard, Doubtful and Loss based on the overdue status and other 
qualitative factors.
4.28. DERIVATIVES
MB enters in currency forward contracts and swap contracts to facilitate customers to transfer, 
modify or mitigate foreign exchange risk or other market risks, and also for the business purpose 
of MB.
Currency forward contracts
The currency forward contracts are commitments to settle in cash on a pre-determined future date 
based on the difference between pre-determined exchange rates, and the notional amount of the 
contracts. The currency forward contracts are recognized at nominal value at the transaction date 
and are revalued periodically. Gains or losses from revaluation are recognized in the consolidated 
income statement.
Swap contracts
The swap contracts are commitments to settle in cash on a pre-determined future date based on 
the difference between pre-determined exchange rates and the notional principal amount of the 
contracts or commitments to settle interest based on a floating rate or a fixed rate calculated on 
the notional amount and in a given period. 
The currency swap contracts are revalued periodically. Gains or losses realized or unrealized are 
recognized in the consolidated income statement. 
Differences in interest rate swaps are recognized in the consolidated income statement on an 
accrual basis.
4.29. EARNINGS PER SHARE
MB presents basic earnings per share for ordinary shares. Basic earnings per share amounts are 
calculated by dividing net profit or loss after tax for the year attributable to ordinary shareholders 
of MB (after adjusting for the bonus and welfare fund) by the weighted average number of ordinary 
shares outstanding during the year.
If the shares issued during the year only change the number of shares without changing the total 
equity, MB will adjust the weighted average number of ordinary shares currently circulated to the 
previous period presented on the consolidated financial statements, resulting in a corresponding 
adjustment of the opening balance of the basic earnings per shares.
4.30. EMPLOYEE BENEFITS
4.30.1. Post-employment benefits 
Post-employment benefits are paid to retired employees of MB in Vietnam by the Social Insurance 
Agency of the Ministry of Labor, Invalids and Social Affairs. MB is required to contribute to these 
post-employment benefits by paying social insurance and occupational accident and disease 
insurance at the rate of 17% of the employee’s basic monthly salary. Other than that, MB has no 
further obligation.
4.30.2. Voluntary resignation benefits
The Bank has the obligation, under Article 46 of the Vietnam Labour Law 45/2019/QH14 effective 
from 1 January 2021, to pay allowance arising from voluntary resignation of employees who fully 
meet the requirements of relevant laws and regulations, equal to one-half month’s salary for each 
year of employment up to 31 December 2008 plus salary allowances (if any). The average monthly 
salary used in this calculation is the average monthly salary of the latest six-month period up to 
the resignation date.
4.30.3. Unemployment benefits
According to Circular No. 28/2015/TT-BLDTBXH providing guidance for Decree No. 28/2015/
ND-CP dated 12 March 2015 on unemployment insurance, from 1 January 2009, MB is required 
to contribute to the unemployment insurance at the rate of 1% of salary and wage fund of 
unemployment insurance joiners and deduct 1% of monthly salary and wage of each employee to 
contribute to the unemployment insurance.
4.31. SEGMENT REPORTING
A segment is a separate unit of MB which participates in providing relevant products and services 
(segments categorized by business sectors) or providing products and services in a certain 
economic environment (segments categorized by geographical regions). Each segment bears 
unique risks and gains different benefits. The fundamental segment report form of MB is based 
on business sectors.

MB has the obligation to pay corporate income tax (“CIT”) at the rate of 20% of taxable profits in 
Vietnam according to Circular No. 78/2014/TT-BTC which became effective from 2 August 2014, 
guiding the implementation of Decree No.218/2013/ND-CP dated 26 December 2013 issued by the 
Government on the Law on Corporate Income Tax.
For the Bank’s branch in Cambodia, MB shall calculate and determine its CIT in compliance with 
Cambodian regulations on corporate income tax. According to the Tax Act dated 8 January 1997, 
the corporate income tax of the Bank’s branch in Cambodia is determined to be the greater of the 
minimum tax payable determined by 1% of total revenue (including value added tax) and 20% of 
profits earned. CIT of the Bank’s branch in Cambodia for the fiscal year ended 31 December 2021 
is defined as 20% of profits earned.
For the Bank’s branch in Laos, MB shall calculate and determine its CIT in accordance with the 
income tax regulations in Laos. According to the Tax Ordinance No. 67 dated 18 June 2019 issued 
by the Lao P.D.R Parliament and became effective from 17 February 2020, CIT of the branch is 
defined as 20% of the profit.
MB’s tax reports are subject to examination by the tax authorities. Because the application of 
tax laws and regulations to many types of transactions is susceptible to varying interpretations, 
amount reported in the consolidated financial statements could be changed at a later date upon 
final determination of the tax authorities.
Current corporate income tax payables are determined based on taxable income of the period. 
Taxable income differs from the one reported in the consolidated income statement since taxable

44.
FINANCIAL RISK 
MANAGEMENT 
POLICIES
This section provides information of MB’s exposure to risks and describes the methods used by the 
Management to control risks. The most important types of financial risks to which MB is exposed 
are credit risk, liquidity risk and market risk.
MB’s orientation is to become a diversified financial group. Therefore, the use of financial 
instruments, including funding from customers (including deposit and valuable papers issued) 
and investments in high quality financial assets has become key activities to help MB gain 
necessary interest rate gaps. From the risk management perspective, MB is required to maintain 
the structure of assets, liabilities and equity (including balance sheet items and off-balance sheet 
items) for the purpose of ensuring safety and mitigating risks in banking activities. In addition, MB 
has invested in securities or granted credit facilities to other banks. The risks related to currency 
exchange and interest rates have been managed through applying of position limits to restrict 
over-concentration and simultaneously participating in activities with balancing impact to 
minimise risks. By holding various assets being high quality financial instruments, the structure 
of MB’s interim consolidated balance sheet would be able to protect MB from significant risks 
during its business processes and ensure liquidity. In addition, MB has been also involved in many 
derivatives transactions related to financial instruments such as currency forward commitments, 
currency swap commitments, and cross currency swap commitments for the purpose of managing 
interest rate risk and currency risk.
In the process of credit risk management, MB has adopted the Credit Handbook which provides in 
details the lending policies and procedures as well as implementation guidance on standardisation 
of MB’s credit activities. Liquidity risk is limited by holding appropriate amounts of cash and cash 
equivalents as demand deposits (“Nostro”), term deposits at the SB Vand other credit institutions 
and valuable papers. The safety ratios with risk factors taken into account are also used to manage 
liquidity risk. MB has regularly assessed interest rate gaps, compared to the gaps of domestic 
markets and international markets to make timely adjustments. In addition, the application of 
internal risk management processes has become more efficient owing to the deployment of 
Centralised Capital Management System and Centralised Payment System in which all capital 
and payment transactions of MB are executed by the Head Office. Such centralisation has also 
helped MB to monitor capital movements more effectively and reduce any possible errors and 
unnecessarily complicated procedures.

INTEREST RATE 
RISK
MB’s operations are subject to the risk of interest rate fluctuations to the extent that interest-
earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities mature at different times or in different amounts. 
Some assets have indefinite maturities or interest rate sensitivities and are not readily matched 
with specific liabilities.
The following table show MB’s assets and liabilities categorised by effective interest re-pricing 
period or maturity date and the effective interest rates as at the reporting date.
The effective interest rate re-pricing term is the remaining period from the reporting date to the 
latest interest rate re-pricing date of assets and liabilities items. The following assumptions and 
conditions are applied in the analysis of the effective interest rate re-pricing term of assets and 
liabilities of MB:
•	 Cash, gold, silver and gems; long-term investments and other assets (including fixed assets and 
some other assets) are classified as non-interest bearings;
•	 Deposits at the State Bank are classified as demand deposits, therefore effective interest re-
pricing term is classified as up to one month;
•	 Securities held for trading are classified as up to one month;
•	 The effective interest rate re-pricing term of investment securities and trading securities is 
determined as follows:
‐‐ Items with fixed interest for the duration of the contract: The effective interest rate re-pricing 
term is based on the actual maturity date from the date of the consolidated financial 
statements;
‐‐ Items with floating interest rates: The effective interest rate re-pricing term is based on the 
latest interest rate re-pricing date from the date of the consolidated financial statements;
‐‐ Investment securities and trading securities which are equity securities are classified as non-
interest bearings.
•	 The effective interest rate re-pricing term of deposits and loans to credit institutions, loans to 
customers granted and trusted for granting; due from the Government and the State Bank; 
deposits and loans from credit institutions; customers’ deposits; other borrowed and entrusted 
funds and valuable papers issued are determined as follows:
‐‐ Items with fixed interest rates for the duration of the contract: The effective interest rate re-
pricing term is based on the actual maturity date from the date of the consolidated balance 
sheet;
‐‐ Items with floating interest rate: The effective interest rate re-pricing term is based on the 
latest interest rate re-pricing date from the date of the consolidated balance sheet;
•	 ►Other liabilities are classified as non-interest bearings.

CURRENCY RISK

foreign exchange rates. MB was incorporated and operates in Vietnam, with VND as its reporting 
currency. The major currency in which MB transacts is VND. MB’s loans and advances to customers 
were mainly denominated in VND and USD. However, some of MB’s other assets are in currencies 
other than VND and USD. MB’s management has set limits on positions by currency based on the 
internal risk assessment and regulations of the SBV. Positions are monitored on a daily basis and 
hedging strategies used to ensure positions are maintained within established limits.

LIQUIDITY RISK
Liquidity risk arises in MB’s funding activities in general and in the management of positions. It 
includes both the risk of being unable to fund assets at appropriate maturities and rates and the 
risk of being unable to liquidate an asset at a reasonable price and in an appropriate time frame.
MB adopts a risk measurement method that is appropriate to its operation scale and the 
availability of the information system, ensuring to meet the requirements for the risk mitigation. 
It includes indicators related to cash flows, ability of capital mobilisation, and ability of asset 
liquidity of MB.  MB also has a designated unit focusing on obtaining update domestic and foreign 
economic information, which directly affects MB’s trading book and business strategies, as well as 
on forecasting movements of market factors such as the foreign exchange rate, interest rate and 
gold price for timely risk warnings. MB also establishes and applies a limit system and decision 
authority at each level based on results of risk measurement for each category.

The following assumptions and conditions are applied in the analysis of the maturity period of

•	 Balances at the State Bank are classified as demand deposits, including compulsory reserves. 
The balance of compulsory deposits depends on the composition and terms of customer 
deposits at MB;
•	 The maturity period of investment securities and trading securities which are debt securities is 
calculated based on the maturity date of each type of securities;
•	 Trading securities which are equity securities are classified into securities with term up to one 
month;
•	 The maturity period of deposits and loans to credit institutions and customers is determined 
based on the maturity date of the specified contract. Actual maturity dates may vary due 
to extended loan agreements. In addition, loans to customers are presented in original value 
excluding provisions;
•	 The maturity period of capital contribution is determined as having term from (1) year to (5) 
years since these investments have no maturity date;
•	 Deposits and borrowings from credit institutions and customers’ deposits are determined based 
on the nature of these items or the maturity date on the contract. Vostro accounts and demand 
deposits are under transaction as required by customers and are therefore classified as demand 
deposits. The maturity period for borrowings and term deposits is determined based on the 
maturity date on the contract. In reality, these accounts may have been renewed and therefore 
have been maintained longer than the original maturity date; and
•	 The maturity period of fixed assets is determined as having term from (1) to (5) years.
